records.source: וַיְהִי֩ דְבַר־יְהוָ֨ה אֵלַ֜י בַּשָּׁנָ֤ה הַתְּשִׁיעִית֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִ֔י בֶּעָשׂ֥וֹר לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And was [the] word of Yahweh to me in the year the ninth, in the month the tenth, on the tenth of the month, saying:
pieces: On the tenth day of the tenth month of the ninth year, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.1: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, saying:

R.1: On the tenth day of the tenth month, in the ninth year of our exile, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: the ninth year, the tenth month, the tenth day: the day the siege of Jerusalem began, in January 588 BC
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 25:1, Jeremiah 39:1 and 52:4 give the same date, counted by King Zedekiah's reign, for the day Nebuchadnezzar's army began the siege of Jerusalem. Zedekiah began to reign in the year Jehoiachin was exiled, so Ezekiel's count gives the same year. The date falls in the winter of 589-588 BC, usually put in January 588 BC. After the exile the day was kept as a fast, "the fast of the tenth month" (Zechariah 8:19).

decisions.choice: in the ninth year of our exile
decisions.reason: As in 20:1, Readable says what the years are counted from and puts the day first. The formula "The word of the LORD came to me" keeps the Jeremiah wording at each level.

records.heading: The pot on the fire

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם כְּתָב־לְךָ֙ אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם הַיּ֔וֹם אֶת־עֶ֖צֶם הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה סָמַ֤ךְ מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֙ אֶל־יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בְּעֶ֖צֶם הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: Son of man, write for yourself the name of the day, this very day; has leaned [the] king of Babylon against Jerusalem on this very day.
pieces: Son of man, write down today's date, this very date. The king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem on this very day.

L.2: Son of man, write down for yourself the name of the day, this very day; the king of Babylon has laid hold of Jerusalem on this very day.

R.2: Son of man, write down today's date. Today the king of Babylon has begun to attack Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: write down the date: a record that will show the word came from God
decisions.reason: Ezekiel lived in Babylonia, hundreds of miles from Jerusalem, and had no way of knowing what happened there that day. The written date would show, when the news came (33:21), that the LORD had told him.

decisions.choice: laid hold of: leaned on, closed in on: began the siege
decisions.reason: The verb means to lean or press on something. Here it means that the army has closed in on the city (compare Psalm 88:8).

decisions.choice: today's date; laid siege (B); begun to attack (R)
alternatives: the name of the day; laid hold of
decisions.reason: "The name of the day" means its date. Balanced and Readable say so, and say what "laid hold of" means here (m2).

records.source: וּמְשֹׁ֤ל אֶל־בֵּית־הַמֶּ֨רִי֙ מָשָׁ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה שְׁפֹ֤ת הַסִּיר֙ שְׁפֹ֔ת וְגַם־יְצֹ֥ק בּ֖וֹ מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And speak to [the] house of rebellion a parable and say to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Set on the pot, set [it] on, and also pour into it water.
pieces: Tell the rebellious house a parable. Say to them, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Put on the pot, put it on, and pour water into it.

L.3: And speak a parable to the house of rebellion and say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Set on the pot, set [it] on, and also pour water into it.

R.3: Tell these people who refuse to obey a story with a hidden meaning. Say to them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Put the cooking pot on the fire. Put it on, and pour water into it.

decisions.choice: a parable: a picture with a meaning to be worked out
decisions.reason: The word is the one the people used to dismiss Ezekiel in 21:5. Here the LORD gives them one, and explains it himself (verses 6-14).

decisions.choice: the song of the pot (verses 3-5): a cooking song turned into a picture of judgment
decisions.reason: Verses 3b-5 have short, rhythmic commands, like a work song sung over the cooking. The pot is Jerusalem and the meat its people, as the leaders had boasted in 11:3: "This city is the pot, and we are the meat". There they meant that they were safe inside the city; here the pot is set on the fire.

decisions.choice: the house of rebellion: a people that refuses to obey
decisions.reason: This is the book's name for Israel; see the note at 2:5.

decisions.choice: house of rebellion (L); rebellious house (B); people who refuse to obey (R); a story with a hidden meaning (R)
decisions.reason: The name follows the wording set for Ezekiel. Readable explains "parable" and says that the pot is a cooking pot set on the fire. The song of verses 3-5 is set as prose, with the rest of the chapter.

records.source: אֱסֹ֤ף נְתָחֶ֨יהָ֙ אֵלֶ֔יהָ כָּל־נֵ֥תַח ט֖וֹב יָרֵ֣ךְ וְכָתֵ֑ף מִבְחַ֥ר עֲצָמִ֖ים מַלֵּֽא׃
records.gloss: Gather its pieces into it, every piece good, thigh and shoulder; [with the] choice of bones fill [it].
pieces: Put the pieces of meat in it, all the good pieces, the thigh and the shoulder; fill it with the choicest bones.

L.4: Gather its pieces into it, every good piece, thigh and shoulder; fill [it] with choice bones.

R.4: Put in the pieces of meat, all the best pieces, the thighs and the shoulders. Fill it with the best bones.

decisions.choice: the best pieces: the leading people of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The good cuts stand for the city's leaders and people, who thought themselves the choice meat kept safe in the pot (11:3, 7-11).

records.source: מִבְחַ֤ר הַצֹּאן֙ לָק֔וֹחַ וְגַ֛ם דּ֥וּר הָעֲצָמִ֖ים תַּחְתֶּ֑יהָ רַתַּ֣ח רְתָחֶ֔יהָ גַּם־בָּשְׁל֥וּ עֲצָמֶ֖יהָ בְּתוֹכָֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: [The] choice of the flock take, and also pile the bones under it; boil its boiling; also its bones are cooked in its midst.
pieces: Take the best of the flock, and pile the bones under the pot. Bring it to a rolling boil, and cook the bones in it.

L.5: Take the choice of the flock, and also pile the bones under it; boil it well; let its bones also be cooked in it.

R.5: Use the best animals from the flock. Pile the bones under the pot to burn. Boil the water hard, and cook the bones in the pot.

decisions.choice: pile the bones under it: bones used as fuel, or a pile of wood
alternatives: "pile the logs under it" (reading a very similar word for "wood", as in verse 10)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the bones", which may mean bones burned as fuel under the pot. Many think a word for "wood" was meant, since the words look alike and verse 10 speaks of piling wood. The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: to burn
decisions.reason: Readable says why the bones are put under the pot (m1).

records.source: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה אוֹי֮ עִ֣יר הַדָּמִים֒ סִ֚יר אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֶלְאָתָ֣ה בָ֔הּ וְחֶ֨לְאָתָ֔הּ לֹ֥א יָצְאָ֖ה מִמֶּ֑נָּה לִנְתָחֶ֤יהָ לִנְתָחֶ֨יהָ֙ הוֹצִיאָ֔הּ לֹא־נָפַ֥ל עָלֶ֖יהָ גּוֹרָֽל׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Woe, city of bloodshed, pot whose rust [is] in it, and whose rust has not gone out of it! Piece by piece bring it out; not has fallen on it a lot.
pieces: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Woe to the city of bloodshed, the pot that is crusted with rust, whose rust has not come off! Empty it piece by piece, without casting lots for any of it.

L.6: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Woe, city of bloodshed, pot whose rust [is] in it, and whose rust has not gone out of it! Piece by piece bring it out; no lot has fallen on it.

R.6: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: How terrible it will be for the city of murderers! It is like a pot crusted with rust that will not come off. Take out every piece, one by one, without choosing among them.

decisions.choice: rust: the corrosion that crusts a metal pot
decisions.reason: The word is found only in this passage. It is usually taken as the rust or corrosion on a bronze pot (verse 11), a picture of the city's guilt that cannot be scrubbed away.

decisions.choice: piece by piece, with no lot cast: all the people taken out, with no choice of who is spared
decisions.reason: Lots were cast to divide captives (Joel 4:3; Obadiah 11). Here there is no choosing: every piece comes out, as the people of Jerusalem will be killed or taken away without distinction.

decisions.choice: Woe (L); Woe to (B); How terrible it will be for (R); the city of murderers (R)
decisions.reason: The cry follows the wording set for the prophets' "woe". Readable says what "city of bloodshed" means, as in 22:2.

records.heading: Woe to the city of bloodshed

records.source: כִּ֤י דָמָהּ֙ בְּתוֹכָ֣הּ הָיָ֔ה עַל־צְחִ֥יחַ סֶ֖לַע שָׂמָ֑תְהוּ לֹ֤א שְׁפָכַ֨תְהוּ֙ עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ לְכַסּ֥וֹת עָלָ֖יו עָפָֽר׃
records.gloss: For her blood in her midst is; on a bare rock she placed it; she did not pour it on the ground to cover over it dust.
pieces: For the blood she shed is still within her; she spilled it on bare rock; she did not pour it on the ground where dust would cover it.

L.7: For her blood is in her midst; she put it on a bare rock; she did not pour it out on the ground to cover it with dust.

R.7: The blood of those she murdered is still there in the city. She poured it out on bare rock. She did not pour it on the ground, where the dirt would cover it.

decisions.choice: blood not covered with dust: blood left open to cry for vengeance
decisions.reason: The law said that the blood of a hunted animal must be covered with earth (Leviticus 17:13). Blood left uncovered was thought to cry out to God, as Abel's did (Genesis 4:10; Job 16:18; Isaiah 26:21). Jerusalem did not even hide its murders.

records.source: לְהַעֲל֤וֹת חֵמָה֙ לִנְקֹ֣ם נָקָ֔ם נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת־דָּמָ֖הּ עַל־צְחִ֣יחַ סָ֑לַע לְבִלְתִּ֖י הִכָּסֽוֹת׃פ
records.gloss: To bring up wrath, to take vengeance, I have put her blood on a bare rock, so that it not be covered.
pieces: To stir up wrath and take vengeance, I have set her blood on bare rock, where it cannot be covered.

L.8: To bring up wrath, to take vengeance, I have put her blood on a bare rock, so that it will not be covered.

R.8: I have left the blood she shed on the bare rock, where it cannot be covered, so that my anger will be stirred and I will punish her.

decisions.choice: I have put her blood on the rock: God leaves the evidence uncovered for judgment
decisions.reason: What the city did by its shamelessness, God now uses as evidence. The blood lies in plain view so that justice must be done.

decisions.choice: the act first, then the purpose
decisions.reason: Readable says what God did first and then why.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה א֖וֹי עִ֣יר הַדָּמִ֑ים גַּם־אֲנִ֖י אַגְדִּ֥יל הַמְּדוּרָֽה׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Woe, city of bloodshed! Also I will make great the pile.
pieces: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Woe to the city of bloodshed! I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will make the pile of wood high.

L.9: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Woe, city of bloodshed! I too will make the pile great.

R.9: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: How terrible it will be for the city of murderers! I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will pile the wood high.

decisions.choice: the pile: the heap of wood for the fire
decisions.reason: The word is used for a pile of wood for burning (Isaiah 30:33). God himself now builds the fire under the pot.

records.source: הַרְבֵּ֤ה הָעֵצִים֙ הַדְלֵ֣ק הָאֵ֔שׁ הָתֵ֖ם הַבָּשָׂ֑ר וְהַרְקַח֙ הַמֶּרְקָחָ֔ה וְהָעֲצָמ֖וֹת יֵחָֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: Heap on the logs, kindle the fire, cook well the meat, and mix the spices, and the bones let them be burned.
pieces: Pile on the logs, light the fire, cook the meat well, mix in the spices, and let the bones be charred.

L.10: Heap on the logs, kindle the fire, cook the meat through, and mix in the spices, and let the bones be burned.

R.10: Pile on the wood and light the fire. Boil the meat until it is done, and mix in the spices. Let the bones burn.

decisions.choice: mix in the spices: an uncertain phrase
decisions.reason: The verb and noun come from a word for mixing spices or ointment, so "mix the spices" is the most direct reading. Others read the words as boiling the broth away, which fits the burning bones and the emptied pot of verse 11.

decisions.choice: the bones burned: the cooking goes on until nothing is left
decisions.reason: The picture moves from a meal to a burning: the contents are destroyed, as Jerusalem was burned (2 Kings 25:9).

records.source: וְהַעֲמִידֶ֥הָ עַל־גֶּחָלֶ֖יהָ רֵקָ֑ה לְמַ֨עַן תֵּחַ֜ם וְחָ֣רָה נְחֻשְׁתָּ֗הּ וְנִתְּכָ֤ה בְתוֹכָהּ֙ טֻמְאָתָ֔הּ תִּתֻּ֖ם חֶלְאָתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And set it on its coals empty, so that it may be hot and glow its bronze, and be melted in its midst its uncleanness, be consumed its rust.
pieces: Then set the empty pot on the coals until it is hot and its bronze glows, so that its uncleanness melts inside it and its rust is burned away.

L.11: Then set it empty on its coals, so that it may become hot and its bronze may glow, and its uncleanness may melt within it, its rust be consumed.

R.11: Then put the empty pot on the coals. Let it get so hot that the bronze glows red. Then the dirt inside it will melt, and the rust will be burned off.

decisions.choice: the empty pot on the fire: the city itself purged by burning
decisions.reason: When the people have been taken out (verse 6), the empty city is set on the fire to burn away its uncleanness. Jerusalem was emptied and burned in 586 BC (2 Kings 25:9-11).

records.source: תְּאֻנִ֖ים הֶלְאָ֑ת וְלֹֽא־תֵצֵ֤א מִמֶּ֨נָּה֙ רַבַּ֣ת חֶלְאָתָ֔הּ בְּאֵ֖שׁ חֶלְאָתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Toil! She has wearied; and not goes out from her her great rust; into [the] fire [with] her rust!
pieces: All the effort has been wasted; its thick rust will not come off, not even in the fire.

L.12: [With] toil she has wearied [me]; and her great rust does not go out of her; into the fire [with] her rust!

R.12: But all the work is useless. The thick rust will not come off, even in the fire.

decisions.choice: the effort is wasted; even fire does not remove the rust: the Hebrew is short and obscure
alternatives: "she has wearied herself", the city exhausting itself in vain
decisions.reason: The verse is compressed: "toil, she has wearied; and her great rust does not go out from her; into the fire her rust". The general sense is that every attempt to clean the pot has failed, so the rust must go into the fire. Who is wearied is not said.

records.source: בְּטֻמְאָתֵ֖ךְ זִמָּ֑ה יַ֤עַן טִֽהַרְתִּיךְ֙ וְלֹ֣א טָהַ֔רְתְּ מִטֻּמְאָתֵךְ֙ לֹ֣א תִטְהֲרִי־ע֔וֹד עַד־הֲנִיחִ֥י אֶת־חֲמָתִ֖י בָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: In your uncleanness [is] lewdness; because I cleansed you and you were not clean from your uncleanness, you will not be clean again until I have caused to rest my wrath on you.
pieces: Your uncleanness is your lewdness. Because I tried to cleanse you and you would not be clean from your uncleanness, you will not be clean again until I have satisfied {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath against you.

L.13: In your uncleanness [is] lewdness. Because I cleansed you, and you were not clean from your uncleanness, you will not be clean again until I have brought {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on you to rest.

R.13: Your shameful ways have made you unclean. I tried to make you clean, but you would not become clean. So you will not be clean again until {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger against you is satisfied.

decisions.choice: because I cleansed you: God's earlier attempts to purify his people
decisions.reason: The cleansing is not described. It is most likely the warnings of the prophets and the earlier judgments that should have turned the city back (Jeremiah 6:29-30). The verb can describe an attempt that failed.

decisions.choice: until I have brought my wrath to rest: until my anger is satisfied
decisions.reason: The same words are used in 5:13, 16:42 and 21:22.

decisions.choice: tried to cleanse (B); tried to make you clean (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain that the cleansing failed (m1). The address changes here to "you", the city itself.

records.source: אֲנִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ בָּאָ֣ה וְעָשִׂ֔יתִי לֹֽא־אֶפְרַ֥ע וְלֹא־אָח֖וּס וְלֹ֣א אֶנָּחֵ֑ם כִּדְרָכַ֤יִךְ וְכַעֲלִילוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ שְׁפָט֔וּךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה׃פ
records.gloss: I, Yahweh, have spoken; it is coming, and I will do [it]; I will not hold back, and I will not pity, and I will not relent; according to your ways and according to your deeds they will judge you, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken. The time has come, and I will act. I will not hold back; I will not show pity; I will not change {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mind. You will be judged by your ways and your deeds, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.14: I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken; it is coming, and I will do [it]. I will not hold back, and I will not pity, and I will not relent; according to your ways and according to your deeds they will judge you, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.14: I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken. The time has come, and I will do what I said. I will not hold back. I will not feel sorry for you or change {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mind. You will be judged for the way you have lived and the things you have done, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: they will judge you: the Hebrew text
alternatives: "I will judge you" (some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient versions)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "they will judge you", the subject left general, much like a passive. Some manuscripts and versions have "I will judge you", which fits the rest of the verse. Either way the judgment is the LORD's.

decisions.choice: I will not hold back, pity or relent: the judgment is fixed
decisions.reason: The three verbs close every way of escape. God's word and deed belong together, as in 17:24 and 22:14.

decisions.choice: You will be judged
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the general "they" as a passive (m1).

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And was [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.15: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: the formula as in Jeremiah
decisions.reason: A new message begins: the death of Ezekiel's wife (verses 15-27).

records.heading: The death of Ezekiel's wife

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הִנְנִ֨י לֹקֵ֧חַ מִמְּךָ֛ אֶת־מַחְמַ֥ד עֵינֶ֖יךָ בְּמַגֵּפָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א תִסְפֹּד֙ וְלֹ֣א תִבְכֶּ֔ה וְל֥וֹא תָב֖וֹא דִּמְעָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Son of man, behold, I [am] taking from you [the] delight of your eyes with a stroke; but not shall you lament, and not shall you weep, and not shall come your tears.
pieces: Son of man, I am about to take away from you the delight of your eyes with one blow. Yet you must not mourn or weep or shed any tears.

L.16: Son of man, see, I am about to take from you the delight of your eyes with a stroke; yet you shall not lament, and you shall not weep, and your tears shall not come.

R.16: Son of man, I am going to take away suddenly the one who is the joy of your life. But you must not mourn for her. Do not cry or shed any tears.

decisions.choice: the delight of your eyes: Ezekiel's wife
decisions.reason: Verse 18 says that his wife died. The same words are used in verse 21 for the temple and in verse 25 for the people's sons and daughters: what Ezekiel loses pictures what Jerusalem will lose.

decisions.choice: with a stroke: by a sudden death
decisions.reason: The word is used for a blow from God, often a plague (Numbers 14:37; 17:13). Here it means a sudden death, without saying how.

decisions.choice: lament, weep, shed tears: the public mourning expected for the dead
decisions.reason: Mourning was loud and public, with wailing and weeping (Genesis 23:2; 2 Samuel 1:12). Jeremiah was also told not to mourn, as a sign (Jeremiah 16:5-7).

decisions.choice: the one who is the joy of your life; mourn for her
decisions.reason: Readable says what the phrase means, and says "her", since verse 18 shows that his wife is meant.

records.source: הֵאָנֵ֣ק׀דֹּ֗ם מֵתִים֙ אֵ֣בֶל לֹֽא־תַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה פְאֵֽרְךָ֙ חֲב֣וֹשׁ עָלֶ֔יךָ וּנְעָלֶ֖יךָ תָּשִׂ֣ים בְּרַגְלֶ֑יךָ וְלֹ֤א תַעְטֶה֙ עַל־שָׂפָ֔ם וְלֶ֥חֶם אֲנָשִׁ֖ים לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Groan, be silent; [for the] dead mourning do not make; your turban bind on you, and your sandals put on your feet, and do not cover over [the] mustache, and [the] bread of men do not eat.
pieces: Groan quietly; do not observe mourning for the dead. Keep your turban tied on and your sandals on your feet. Do not cover your upper lip, and do not eat the bread that others bring to mourners.

L.17: Groan in silence; do not make mourning for the dead; bind your turban on you, and put your sandals on your feet, and do not cover [your] upper lip, and do not eat the bread of men.

R.17: Groan quietly, but do not hold any funeral rites for the dead. Keep your turban on your head and your sandals on your feet. Do not cover the lower part of your face to mourn, and do not eat the food that friends bring to people who are mourning.

decisions.choice: turban, sandals, upper lip: the signs of mourning Ezekiel must not show
decisions.reason: Mourners took off their headdress and went barefoot (2 Samuel 15:30; Isaiah 20:2) and covered the lower face (Leviticus 13:45; Micah 3:7). Ezekiel is to dress as on any ordinary day.

decisions.choice: the bread of men: the meal neighbors brought to mourners
alternatives: "the bread of mourners" (reading a similar word, as in Hosea 9:4)
decisions.reason: Friends and neighbors brought food to a house of mourning (Jeremiah 16:7; 2 Samuel 3:35). The Hebrew has "bread of men"; many read the very similar "bread of mourners", which gives the same sense.

decisions.choice: do not hold any funeral rites
alternatives: do not make mourning for the dead
decisions.reason: Readable says what the mourning was, and explains the upper lip and the bread (m1, m2).

records.source: וָאֲדַבֵּ֤ר אֶל־הָעָם֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וַתָּ֥מָת אִשְׁתִּ֖י בָּעָ֑רֶב וָאַ֥עַשׂ בַּבֹּ֖קֶר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צֻוֵּֽיתִי׃
records.gloss: And I spoke to the people in the morning, and died my wife in the evening; and I did in the morning as I was commanded.
pieces: So in the morning I spoke to the people, and that evening my wife died. The next morning I did as I had been commanded.

L.18: And I spoke to the people in the morning, and my wife died in the evening; and I did in the morning as I had been commanded.

R.18: I spoke to the people in the morning. That evening my wife died. The next morning I did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told me to do.

decisions.choice: my wife died: the only mention of Ezekiel's wife
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's wife is not named and is mentioned nowhere else. Like Hosea's marriage and Jeremiah's being forbidden to marry (Hosea 1-3; Jeremiah 16:1-4), the prophet's own life becomes part of the message.

decisions.choice: I spoke to the people in the morning: what he said is not told
alternatives: a morning of ordinary speaking, before the word of verse 16 came
decisions.reason: The verse is very brief. It may mean that Ezekiel told the people the LORD's word of verses 16-17 that morning, before his wife died in the evening.

decisions.choice: what the LORD had told me
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who gave the command.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ אֵלַ֖י הָעָ֑ם הֲלֹֽא־תַגִּ֥יד לָ֨נוּ֙ מָה־אֵ֣לֶּה לָּ֔נוּ כִּ֥י אַתָּ֖ה עֹשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: And said to me the people, Will you not tell us what these [are] to us, that you [are] doing?
pieces: Then the people asked me, "Will you not tell us what these things you are doing mean for us?"

L.19: And the people said to me, "Will you not tell us what these [things mean] for us, that you are doing?"

R.19: The people asked me, "Why are you acting like this? Tell us what it means for us."

decisions.choice: the people ask what the sign means
decisions.reason: As with the groaning of 21:12, the strange behavior makes people ask, and the question opens the way for the message (12:9).

decisions.choice: narrative dialogue in double quotes
decisions.reason: This is dialogue in Ezekiel's narrative, so it takes quotation marks, as prose does. Ezekiel's answer (verses 20-24) also takes them; the LORD's message inside it takes none.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֖ר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם דְּבַ֨ר־יְהוָ֔ה הָיָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And I said to them, [The] word of Yahweh came to me, saying:
pieces: I answered them, "The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.20: And I said to them, "The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

R.20: I told them, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: the formula as in Jeremiah, inside Ezekiel's answer
decisions.reason: The formula keeps its wording at each level. The quotation opened here closes at the end of verse 24.

records.source: אֱמֹ֣ר׀לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ הִנְנִ֨י מְחַלֵּ֤ל אֶת־מִקְדָּשִׁי֙ גְּא֣וֹן עֻזְּכֶ֔ם מַחְמַ֥ד עֵֽינֵיכֶ֖ם וּמַחְמַ֣ל נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם וּבְנֵיכֶ֧ם וּבְנֽוֹתֵיכֶ֛ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲזַבְתֶּ֖ם בַּחֶ֥רֶב יִפֹּֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: Say to [the] house of Israel, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Behold, I [am] profaning my sanctuary, [the] pride of your strength, [the] delight of your eyes, and [the] desire of your soul; and your sons and your daughters whom you left behind by the sword will fall.
pieces: Tell the house of Israel, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am about to profane {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary, the pride of your strength, the delight of your eyes and the desire of your heart. The sons and daughters you left behind will be cut down by the sword.

L.21: Say to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: See, I am about to profane {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary, the pride of your strength, the delight of your eyes and the desire of your soul; and your sons and your daughters, whom you left behind, by the sword will fall.

R.21: Tell the people of Israel, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} temple be made unholy. You are proud of it and trust in its strength. You love to look at it, and you long for it. The sons and daughters you left behind in Jerusalem will be killed with the sword.

decisions.choice: the delight of your eyes: the temple, as Ezekiel's wife was his
decisions.reason: The same words used for Ezekiel's wife (verse 16) are used here for the temple. As he lost what he loved most, so the exiles will lose the temple they were proud of and trusted. "The pride of your strength" is used in Leviticus 26:19 for what God will break.

decisions.choice: the sons and daughters you left behind: family members still in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's hearers had been deported in 597 BC, and many had left children and relatives in Judah (2 Kings 24:14-16).

decisions.choice: the desire of your soul: what you long for
alternatives: what you pity, what you spare
decisions.reason: The noun is rare. It is usually related to a verb for sparing or feeling for something, and so means what one cherishes.

decisions.choice: I am going to let my temple be made unholy. You are proud of it ...
alternatives: I am about to profane my sanctuary, the pride of your strength ...
decisions.reason: Readable says what "profane" means and turns the three titles of the temple into short sentences. It adds "in Jerusalem" for where the children were left (m2).

records.source: וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי עַל־שָׂפָם֙ לֹ֣א תַעְט֔וּ וְלֶ֥חֶם אֲנָשִׁ֖ים לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: And you will do as I have done; over [the] mustache you will not cover, and [the] bread of men you will not eat.
pieces: Then you will do what I have done. You will not cover your upper lip or eat the bread that others bring to mourners.

L.22: And you will do just as I have done: [your] upper lip you will not cover, and the bread of men you will not eat.

R.22: Then you will do what I have done. You will not cover the lower part of your face to mourn or eat the food that friends bring to mourners.

decisions.choice: as I have done: Ezekiel speaks of himself
decisions.reason: Within the answer the speaker shifts from the LORD (verse 21) to Ezekiel, who points to what he did. Verse 24 returns to the LORD speaking of Ezekiel.

decisions.choice: not mourning: the loss will be too great, or come too suddenly, for mourning
alternatives: they will not be allowed to mourn
decisions.reason: The text does not say why the exiles will not mourn. They may be too stunned for the usual rites, or the disaster may be beyond the comfort of mourning. Verse 23 says that they will waste away in their sins.

records.source: וּפְאֵרֵכֶ֣ם עַל־רָאשֵׁיכֶ֗ם וְנַֽעֲלֵיכֶם֙ בְּרַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם לֹ֥א תִסְפְּד֖וּ וְלֹ֣א תִבְכּ֑וּ וּנְמַקֹּתֶם֙ בַּעֲוֺנֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וּנְהַמְתֶּ֖ם אִ֥ישׁ אֶל־אָחִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And your turbans [will be] on your heads, and your sandals on your feet; not will you lament and not will you weep; and you will waste away in your iniquities, and you will groan each to his brother.
pieces: Your turbans will stay on your heads and your sandals on your feet. There will be no mourning or weeping; instead you will waste away because of your guilt and groan to one another.

L.23: And your turbans [will be] on your heads and your sandals on your feet; and you will not lament, and you will not weep; but you will waste away in your iniquities, and you will groan to one another.

R.23: Your turbans will stay on your heads, and you will keep your sandals on. You will not mourn or cry. Instead you will waste away because of your sins and groan to one another.

decisions.choice: waste away in your iniquities: be consumed by guilt and its punishment
decisions.reason: The same words are used in 4:17 and 33:10, and in Leviticus 26:39 for the exiles in the lands of their enemies.

decisions.choice: groan each to his brother: groan to one another
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "each to his brother" means "to one another".

decisions.choice: iniquities (L); guilt (B); sins (R)
decisions.reason: The word follows the wording set for the prophets.

records.source: וְהָיָ֨ה יְחֶזְקֵ֤אל לָכֶם֙ לְמוֹפֵ֔ת כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ בְּבֹאָ֕הּ וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And will be Ezekiel to you a sign; according to all that he has done you will do; when it comes, and you will know that I [am the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: Ezekiel will be a sign for you; you will do just as he has done. When it comes, then you will know that I am the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}."

L.24: And Ezekiel will become for you a sign; according to all that he has done you will do. When it comes, you will know that I [am] the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}."

R.24: Ezekiel will be a sign to you. You will do everything he has done. This will happen. Then you will know that I am the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: Ezekiel will be a sign: the prophet's life as a message
decisions.reason: This is one of only two places where the book names Ezekiel (1:3). The prophet himself is the sign, as in 12:6 and 11.

decisions.choice: you will know that I am the Lord GOD: the refrain
decisions.reason: See the note at 6:7. Here the knowing comes "when it comes": when the news of Jerusalem's fall arrives.

records.source: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֔ם הֲל֗וֹא בְּי֨וֹם קַחְתִּ֤י מֵהֶם֙ אֶת־מָ֣עוּזָּ֔ם מְשׂ֖וֹשׂ תִּפְאַרְתָּ֑ם אֶת־מַחְמַ֤ד עֵֽינֵיהֶם֙ וְאֶת־מַשָּׂ֣א נַפְשָׁ֔ם בְּנֵיהֶ֖ם וּבְנוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you, son of man, will it not be on [the] day [when] I take from them their stronghold, [the] joy of their glory, [the] delight of their eyes, and [the] longing of their soul, their sons and their daughters,
pieces: As for you, son of man, on the day I take from them their stronghold, their joy and glory, the delight of their eyes and the desire of their hearts, and their sons and daughters as well,

L.25: And you, son of man, will it not be on the day when I take from them their stronghold, the joy of their glory, the delight of their eyes and the longing of their soul, their sons and their daughters,

R.25: Son of man, a day is coming when I will take away from them the temple, their strong place, their joy and pride. It is the delight of their eyes and the desire of their hearts. I will take their sons and daughters too.

decisions.choice: their stronghold, their joy, the delight of their eyes: the temple, as in verse 21
decisions.reason: The titles repeat those of verse 21. The temple was the people's refuge and pride.

decisions.choice: will it not be on the day ...: a question that runs on into verses 26-27
decisions.reason: The long sentence asks, in effect, "Is it not so that on that day ...?" and its answer is the promise of verses 26-27.

decisions.choice: the temple
decisions.reason: Readable names the stronghold as the temple (m1) and breaks the long question into statements.

records.heading: A survivor will bring the news

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יָב֥וֹא הַפָּלִ֖יט אֵלֶ֑יךָ לְהַשְׁמָע֖וּת אָזְנָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: on the day the that will come the fugitive to you, to cause to hear [the] ears.
pieces: on that day a survivor will come to tell you the news.

L.26: on that day a fugitive will come to you to make [you] hear [it] with [your] ears.

R.26: On that day someone who has escaped will come and tell you the news.

decisions.choice: a fugitive will come: fulfilled in 33:21
decisions.reason: In 33:21, in the twelfth year of the exile, a man who had escaped from Jerusalem came to Ezekiel and said, "The city has been struck down".

decisions.choice: a survivor (B); someone who has escaped (R)
decisions.reason: The word means someone who escaped the disaster; Balanced and Readable put it in everyday words.

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִפָּ֤תַח פִּ֨יךָ֙ אֶת־הַפָּלִ֔יט וּתְדַבֵּ֕ר וְלֹ֥א תֵֽאָלֵ֖ם ע֑וֹד וְהָיִ֤יתָ לָהֶם֙ לְמוֹפֵ֔ת וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: On the day the that will be opened your mouth with the fugitive, and you will speak and not be silent any longer; and you will be to them a sign, and they will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: On that day your mouth will be opened to the survivor; you will speak and no longer be silent. So you will become a sign for them. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.27: On that day your mouth will be opened with the fugitive, and you will speak and no longer be silent; and you will become a sign for them; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.27: On that day you will be able to speak again. You will talk with the one who escaped and will not be silent any longer. You will be a sign for them. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: your mouth will be opened: the end of Ezekiel's silence
decisions.reason: In 3:26-27 God made Ezekiel unable to speak except when God gave him a word. In 33:22 his mouth was opened on the evening before the survivor arrived. The silence seems to have been a limit on his ordinary speech, not total silence, since he spoke many oracles in between.

decisions.choice: they will know that I am the LORD: the refrain
decisions.reason: The refrain (see 6:7) here closes the first half of the book: once Jerusalem has fallen, the exiles will know that Ezekiel's words were the LORD's.
